Messages.Body:
hi !

something happened during a tournament yesterday.

My predator, playing eurobrujah, put a Camarilla Segregation in play with
Donal O Conor. He then rushed one of my !salubri with Theo Bell. I blocked
with Wolf Valentine, sent him to torpor with 5 aggravated from a gas powered
chainsaw. His turn ended. I untapped, payed the pool for camarilla
segregation. Then i went to diablerize theo bell with Thomas Steed the
Angry. During the diablerie, i asked for the voices of my "allies", which
means grand predator and grand prey. Alas, as my gandprey wasn't agreeing
for throwing the edge in my favor, i said "okay, as no one will support me
in the vote, i decide to burn Thomas Steed to get rid of the Camarilla
segregation"
Then every other player said i couldn't do that. Some of them referred to
the diablerie being "atomic" and thus nothing could happen once the blood
hunt was called. The judge agreed to their complaints.

But i maintain my opinion. As Camarilla segregation states "Any Methuselah
may burn this card by burning a Non-Camarilla vampire he or she controls
during his or her minion phase." I can't see anything prohibiting me from
burning Thomas steed the minute after i do the diablerie to burn the
camarilla segregation.

So LSJ ?? =)

reyda
(!salubri rules anyway ;) )

From the Online Rulebook:

When a vampire commits diablerie, any Methuselah may call for a referendum to
see if a blood hunt will be called on the diablerist. If the referendum passes,
a blood hunt is called, and the diablerist is burned. This referendum is not an
action, and no political action card is required. Since this is not an action,
it cannot be blocked, and action modifiers and reaction cards cannot be played.
Otherwise, this referendum is handled just like any other.

In a normal referendum, you could for example:

#1. Tap the Barrens to discard (though of course you wouldn't draw up till
after the referendum).

#2. Tap the Fragment to draw two cards and discard (important if you're trying
to look for a PA to discard for a vote).

#3. Use effects such as Grendel's and Tusk's to look at the top card of your
crypt/library.

#4. Tap the Slaughterhouse to burn the top 2 cards of your prey's library.

#5. Burn counters off of a Temptation to gain control of a vampire (useful if
you suddenly realize you need that vampire's votes).

#6. (Discussed earlier). Burn Disarm on a vampire by burning 3 blood and/or
burn a vampire to burn Judgement: Camarilla Segregration.

* Other examples are also possible.

So since none of these effects "gain votes" (directly), they can't be used
during a Blood Hunt though they can be used during a normal referendum?

Seems like the "Otherwise, this referendum is handled just like any other." is
far from the truth...

Halcyan 2

The atomic ruling in itself is confusing and artificial. However, lumping in
the Blood Hunt as part of the diablerie makes it unclear why you cannot play,
for example, Madrigal during the Blood Hunt vote. If, for example, a vampire
is diablerized as an action (as opposed to with Amaranth, for which this would
probably still apply), and the entire resolution of the successful diablerie
action includes the Blood Hunt as well, then Madrigal should be playable, as it
must be played during a referendum, and can be played as a reaction/action
modifier. So, if the whole process is atomic, then it all occurs during the
resolution of the action (the same time that a referendum called by a political
action would occur).

The way that I always thought it was played before was that the diablerie
happens, with all effects involved. Then, the action is completed, and at this
point another Methuselah can call a Blood Hunt. No other effects could be used
before the Blood Hunt was called, but once the Blood Hunt was either called or
not called (i.e. everyone declines to call it), the diablerie action was over,
and a separate referendum, not associated with any action, was then called.
Restricting certain types of effects but not others is certainly more
artificial than restricting either all effects or no effects.

If the Blood Hunt, from beginning to end, is part of the diablerie, then if the
diabelerie is the resolution of a diablerie action, then what is the rationale
for not being able to use action modifiers and reactions during it? Assuming

"Chris Berger" <ark...@ugcs.caltech.edu> wrote in message news:<w05q8.147575$Yv2.45267@rwcrnsc54>...

I agree with Chris on his point. I have always viewed, and taught,
that Blood Hunt is a possible consequence of diablerie. You could
play whatever cards (Ritual of the Bitter Rose, etc...) during the
diablerie, but once the diablerie action was finished, then a decision
on whether a Blood Hunt was to be called had to be made immediately
afterward. This would not allow the possibility of other actions
taking place in between the end of the diablerie action and the
decision of a Blood Hunt. I can understand identifying a checklist of
effects that occur during a diablerie, but when would I play a Ritual?
Prior to the movement of step 1 in the list? At the time of step 1
in the list? Or after step 1 in the list?

Once the diablerie action was complete, a Blood Hunt decision would be
reached (to call or not to call...) and if it was called then
political action cards, appropriate permanents and appropriate vampire
specials would apply to the Blood Hunt vote (or referendum).

I have never seen any room for another action to take place between
the diablerie action and the Blood Hunt decision (and possible
resulting vote) as it has always been considered akin to Freak Drive,
but as a verbal reaction only usable by other players after a
successful diablerie action.

Michael Eichler
Prince of Ramstein

Also, as I think you indicated in another post, if the Blood
Hunt happened after diablerie concluded, ie after a diablerie
action were all over and done with, it wouldn't be possible to
play, say, Freak Drive after the Blood Hunt referendum. But
it's also not possible to play Freak Drive *before* the Blood
Hunt referendum, because you're not in the "completed/completing"
part of the action until after the diablerie (bits 1-4) are
done, and if the Blood Hunt follows immediately (terminating
the action), you've closed off that stage.

(Unless you let people do things between diablerie bits 1-4
and the Blood Hunt. But that's (a) bad and (b) contradicts
years of precedent in which it wasn't possible to do anything
with a vampire that had just diablerized before it could get
burned by a Blood Hunt.)

(Also unless I'm wrong about what making the Blood Hunt "after
the action" would do to end-of-diablerie-action timing. I
don't see off the top of my head, though, how it could be
avoided without making new special-exception rules that would
be at least as confusing as the existing rules.)

Ok, gotta look at the big picture. I can agree with that, however,
Ritual of the Bitter Rose is an Action Modifier/Combat card played by
the acting minion while Reform Body is a Reaction/Combat card played
by the player faced with losing a minion by either diablerie or not
being able to heal an excessive amount of aggravated damage during
combat.
Ritual becomes usable when an opposing vampire is being burn by either
diablerie or during combat against the acting vampire.
Reform becomes usable when a vampire is being burned and goes to
torpor instead.

Based upon the text, these cards are to be played when a diablerie
action goes unblocked (therefore, considered a successful action) but
prior to the action's completion. Correct?

However, there are cards (as previously mentioned within this thread)
that are usable during any time (aka. Book of Nod, Barrens, etc.) from
previous clarifications made by you. In the middle of a combat, you
can use the Barrens or Book of Nod. Based upon card text, which
overrides the standard defaults within the rules, of the Judgement:
Camarilla Segregation, it states that the card can be burned by any
Methuselah by burning a non-camarilla vampire during her minion phase.
It does not state that this is an action, it simply states it can be
done during the phase, much the same as Book of Nod or Barrens just
state Tap and (cause this effect). If the problem is someone trying
to burn a vampire that successfully diablerized another vampire and
preventing them from then burning the acting vampire to get rid of a
Judgement: Camarilla Segregation prior to the Blood Hunt, then change
the card. Otherwise, you affect other cards that have nothing to do
in this type of situation.

In short, you are now making the rules override the cards. And in
doing so, it should generate new errata that was previously
unnecessary on several cards that have never created a problem in the
past.

As I understand it, Ritual of the Bitter Rose is played *after*
the diablerie (the whole indivisible thing) goes off, because
it's only usable on a "successful" diablerie and needs to know
how much blood was on the vampire before it got diablerized;
Reform Body is played *before* the (indivisible) diablerie is
resolved, because it prevents any of the diablerie from happening:
the burning, the moving of blood, the moving of equipment, the
Blood Hunt vote.

So RotBR is played in a similar time-phase to Freak Drive (ie
"after" but "within" the action); Reform Body earlier.

> In short, you are now making the rules override the cards. And in
> doing so, it should generate new errata that was previously
> unnecessary on several cards that have never created a problem in the
> past.

True, but it's at least weird and possibly bad to be able to
burn a vampire for Judgment: Camarilla Segregation in the
middle of a Blood Hunt referendum - probably at least as weird
as not being able to use "anytime" effects at all during Blood
Hunt referenda, even though they are generally usable during
"normal" referenda.

And this ruling can probably be replaced by a rule at the next
printing of the rulebook.

Josh

What are all of these corner cases?

Ritual of the Bitter Rose - prior to actual diablerie and removal of
the targeted vampire.
Reform Body - prior to actual diablerie and removal of the targeted
vampire.
Judgement: Camarilla Segregation - The only issue I can see being at
stake here.

On the use of Ritual of the Bitter Rose, I do make use of Ritual of
the Bitter Rose quite often. I can understand how the card is suppose
to be played prior to a diablerie action's conclusion to gain it's
effect. However, as stated in my previous posting I can see no issue
with either Ritual of the Bitter Rose or Reform Body. Both state
within their text when they are suppose to be played, which is prior
to a diablerie action's conclusion. Both deal with a vampire that is
going to be burned, not after the fact. Therefore, a player using
Ritual must play the card prior to the diablerie's enactment to gain
blood for it and all other vampires with the same controller. A
Reform Body must be played prior to the targeted vampire being placed
into the ashheap, per card text: "...Only usable by a vampire being
burned..." to override the normal course of events. It goes to torpor
rather than the ashheap. Whether or not this means all equipment and
retainers on the vampire are lost is another question.
The issue of when a Judgement: Camarilla Segregation is a corner case
that should be dealt with. I do not agree that a vampire should be
allowed to diablerize another vampire and then in the same action burn
itself to remove a J:CS. However, I do not believe making a rules
change is the optimal method of dealing with this corner case
situation. (In fact, I regard a rules change a bigger event than
simple errata, but that is my personal feeling on the matter.) I can
understand the position you are trying to deal with, but wouldn't a
rules clarification which 1) identifies a Blood Hunt as a byproduct of
a diablerie (as it is described within the rules) and 2) identifies a
diablerie action as not being completed until resolution of it's Blood
Hunt issue is resolved, be better and simpler? Heck, how many other
ways can a Blood Hunt be called except through diablerie? (And no,
the action card "Blood Hunt" is not the same thing. One burns a
vampire via a special vote while the other allows every Tom, Dick and
Harry to attack a selected vampire.)

Michael Eichler

Messages.Author: Rodrigo Diaz

Some info on the origin of this word:

(Latin) Atomus: uncut, indivisible.

http://www.hyperdictionary.com/dictionary?define=atom

Originally, atoms were supposed to be indivisible and to consitute the
minimum essential building unit from which all matter was made. Hence,
the use of the word is perfectly correct in this context, although it
is not a colloquial use of "atomic" (generally used regarding nuclear
energy.

Actually, step 5 within the rules (paper copy and on-line) state "...A
Blood Hunt may be called..." So in reality, Raille is correct.
However, in 6.5.6 it states that the calling of a Blood Hunt is not an
action, so that means it is a possible result of a diablerie. I
really believe step 5 should be state, "...Blood Hunt resolution..."
with Tabs (or steps) under it to clarify the what the Blood Hunt
resolution entails.

Now being out of the loop for a while and reading some of these
postings, I am now curious what other changes have occurred that I am
unaware of.
1) Has Fragment of the Book of Nod and The Barrens been modified to
meet the same criteria as Heidelburg Castle?
That is,
a) they can only be used between actions during your turn?
b) or just between actions, no matter whose turn?
2) Or is this clarification of what the new/proposed rules change will
enforce?

I am still at a loss on how something like Husamettin's ability (when
it kicks in) would cloud this issue. What is the big deal with
looking for two master discipline cards at the same time rather than 1
prior to the Blood Hunt determination/resolution and 1 afterward? It
is an inherent ability of the vampire and doesn't require an action
card to perform, just like Blood Hunt doesn't require an action card
to perform. Heck, both result due to a diablerie.

The only card I can see that is vague on when in a player's minion
phase it can be burned. Now as much as I am NOT a fan of errata, I am
surprised this has not be caught before and corrected during the Era
(thanks, Derek) of errata. It has been around a while (Dark
Sovereigns).

Either that, or clarify what the rules currently state. A new ruling
is in effect "errata" on the rules. Either way, we are dealing with
errata, one for the rules or one for the card.

The only other reason that comes to mind as to why new rulings would
come out now would be for their entry into the coming expansion and it
has either already been printed in the new rule books for the
expansion or you are just testing the water (which I somehow doubt).

Michael Eichler
Prince of Ramstein

"Chris Berger" <ark...@ugcs.caltech.edu> wrote in message news:<%l3t8.205855$Yv2.67200@rwcrnsc54>...

> Again, not true. 6.5.5.5 says that a Blood Hunt may be called.
> 6.5.6, which is the actual resolution of the Blood Hunt is
> separate from section 6.5.5 (the diablerie). Thus, according
> to the rules, the Blood Hunt is seperate from the diablerie.

I think, your confusion arises from assuming that the section headings
in the rule book carry some meaning. They do not.

The section headings are only present for making indexing and
reference easier. There is no rule that states: each rulebook section
refers to a separate action/thing.

This is an "interface" problem. You are assuming that the rulebook
itself follows certain conventions that it does not. Perhaps it is a
flaw in the rulebook layout that it can be misinterpreted in this way,
and maybe someone (LSJ) will make a modification in a new edition. A
method would be to rename both 6.5.5 and 6.5.6 to be 6.5.4.1 and
6.5.4.2 respectively, although that may be too many layers.

* lehrbuch

Messages.Author: Andrew S. Davidson
Messages.Body:
On 10 Apr 2002 18:27:54 -0700, lehrbuch wrote:

>I think, your confusion arises from assuming that the section headings
>in the rule book carry some meaning. They do not.
>
>The section headings are only present for making indexing and
>reference easier. There is no rule that states: each rulebook section
>refers to a separate action/thing.

You've got it backwards. LSJ's case rests upon the manner in which
the rulebook is indexed - he draws great significance from the fact
that the sentence "A blood hunt may be called." has the number "5" in
front of it. He has a point but, if you go that way, then the heading
"6.5.6 Blood Hunt" is more significant to my mind - it's bigger and
bolder and has the same status as "6.5.5 Diablerie".

Note that the original Jyhad rulebook didn't use any numbers when
describing Diablerie and the Blood Hunt and seems none the worse for
it. It didn't say whether these things were atomic but neither does
the latest rulebook. If there are some new rules which are outside
the rulebook then they should say what they mean. If something is
atomic then they should define that something precisely.

Do these virtual rules actually exist as a proper rules document
somewhere? LotR has an "expanded rulebook" which only exists as an
online PDF but which is complete and well integrated. Magic has its
Comprehensive Rules. My impression is that VTES just has the printed
rulebook plus a ragbag of FAQ-style rulings. It's not alone in that
but I just want to be sure.

BTW, I notice that the original rules had an action type of "Encounter
a Vampire in Torpor" but this seems to have gone away. That's just an
NRA issue, I suppose, but still seems noteworthy.

Andrew

Messages.Author: Raille
Messages.Body:
http://www.white-wolf.com/VTES/rulebook/rulebook.html#sec6_2_3

6.2.3. Resolve the Action

If the action is successful (all block attempts were
unsuccessful), then the cost of the action is paid,
and the effects of the successful action take place.

6.3.2. The Referendum

If a political action is successful, the referendum
(sometimes referred to as the vote*) is called.

6.5.4. Diablerize a Vampire in Torpor

To have one vampire diablerize another vampire
in torpor, announce the action and tap the acting
vampire. If the action is successful, the victim is
diablerized (see below).

The Key thing being pointed out here is that the action must be
successful before any results can be applied.

Thus in reference to diablery, the action is over once the vampire is
diablerized. The blood hunt should come immediantly after this and is
supported in that role by the current rules.

However, there are a couple interesting things that this leads to.

action over, thus not linked, the Blood hunt cannot make use of AM's and
Reacts.

Look closely at the plotical action. Action over, call the referendum.
Which seems to me to indicate that once the referendum is being voted
on there is no longer an action to support and you cannot use reaction
or AM cards to gain or lose votes.

Weird.

Action Modifier Card: A card that the acting
minion can play to modify the action he is
performing.

Reaction Card: A card played by a
Methuselah's ready, untapped minion in response
to an action taken by a minion controlled by
another Methuselah.

Only a few cards allow the AM or react to but used outside the action,
and those specifically state when they are played on the card text.

So, it seems that LSJ is allowing AM/React to be used in a referendum,
but not on a Blood Hunt referendum, although the rules by strict
definition say other wise.

More rules that need to be fixed, or cards changes (like Dread Gaze) for
they are no longer react/AM cards.

I've never bothered to poke holes into the rules much, but this diablery
thing got me wondering.

So either AM/react should be allowed in both, or disallowed inboth, or I
can see some errata comming on.

Raille

Other people have pointed out the obvious already, but if you want a thematic
sort of reason why you can't do this, most modifiers/reactions are usable during
a referendum which results from a *political action*, while diablerie is a
different sort of action. (Unless, of course, your vampire was blocked while

whatever.

>

This is something that has bothered me too. I think the ambiguity is
between the action being "successful" and being "over". Its a
"success" when its not blocked. Its "over" when the effect has been
fully resolved.

I'm bled. The action succeeded. But its not over until I move my pool
into the blood back.

Similarly, I call a KRC. Its not blocked. The action succeeds. The
"effect" of that successful action is we now have a referendum. But
the action isn't over until the referendum is done and its results are
resolved.

For example, I can't tap Heidelberg during the referendum to get more
blood to play Awe. I can play Awe in the first place because we're
still in the action. So I can modify it. And I can tap Demonstration
because we're inside a "Political Action".

Someone let me know if I'm horribly wrong about this explanation.

-Ben Swainbank

Messages.Body:

Right.

The resolution of the action is: apply the results of the successful action
or enter combat with the blocking minion. [6.2.3]

The resolution is a part of the action (the last part, typically).

I find no rule in the rule book that tells that the political action
is over before the referendum.

A successful action is one that is not blocked [6.2.3]; it need not
be "over" to be successful.

Once successful (i.e., all block attempts are abandoned), then the
action is resolved (i.e., the effects of the action are applied).
[6.2.3]

In the case of a political action, resolving the action involves
conducting a referendum. [6.3]

In particular, action modifiers can be played (subject to the normal
rules on playing cards) [6.3.3], indicating that there is still an
action around to be modified.

Hey Raille - I don't mean to be rude, but I'm getting the idea
that you've never been too familiar with the exact rules of the
game. (That's not necessarily a bad thing, of course.)

Freak Drive has *always* been played after the action succeeds
(meaning after it has gone unblocked and effects have been
applied). The "that is not blocked" text is telling you that
you can only play it, at inferior, if you weren't blocked before
performing the successful action. The "as above, but usable
even if the action is blocked" text spells out that the "blocked"
part is telling you what conditions the card requires to be
playable. The part that tells you *when* to play it is "after
this vampire performs an action". The action has been performed
*after* its effects have been applied, but not when you're still
in the "does anyone block? well then, do you Deflect?" stage
of the action.

You could actually argue that, if you read Freak Drive strictly,
the superior still only works on successful actions, since it
doesn't say "even if the action fails" but only "even if the
action is blocked" - that would mean that the only benefit of
superior Freak Drive would be that you could use it after
being blocked and continuing via Form of Mist or something (and
that inferior Freak Drive wouldn't be usable after a continued-
by-Form-of-Mist action). But intent seems clear enough in the
other direction (that superior Freak Drive is usable on failed
actions that were blocked).

Josh

> Domain of evernight triggers with the effect of being succesful. Not
> after the action is succesful

An action is "successful" when its effects take place, not
before. So if you play an action modifier "when an action is
successful", you play it after the effects take place.

> And scrying is also played as the action succeeds.

Scrying is played "when this vampire successfully bleeds a
Methuselah." That doesn't happen until the bled Meth has
actually burned pool for the bleed, ie once the effects of
the action have been applied.

> So to sum up. Your wrong to assume these cards are played after the
> action is resolved.

No. Really. They are. ;-)

This is another thing that's "always been the way it is". From
the original Jyhad rulebook:

---------
14. SUMMARY OF THE COURSE OF AN ACTION

1) A player's action is declared, and an action card is played if
necessary. The acting minion is tapped.
2) If a Methuselah was directly affected, he or she has the opportunity
to try to block the action. If the action is blocked, the blocking minion
is tapped, and combat ensues (exception: Leave Torpor action, Sec. 16.2).
3) If the action was not directed against a Methuselah, then your prey
may attempt to block the action. If your prey does not block the action,
then your predator may attempt to block the action.
4) If unblocked, the minion's action is successful. The Methuselah must
then pay any cost associated with the action. If the Methuselah cannot pay
the cost, whatever can be paid is paid, and the effects of the unpaid
cards do not take place. Players cannot play the same action modifier card
more than once per action.
---------

You can see at (4) that the action "is successful" when the
Methuselah (or minion) pays the cost of the action. Clearly
any action modifiers played "when an action is successful" then
need to be played after that.

Josh

I still think that the rulebook says that the Blood Hunt is resolved *after*
the diablerie for the following reasons:

- 6.5.5.5 says that a Blood Hunt may be called. 6.5.5 contains the entire
resolution of the successful diablerie, but it does not indicate that the Blood
Hunt is to be resolved as part of the diablerie. It simply indicateds that it
is *called* as part of the diablerie. 6.5.6 outlines the resolution of the
Blood Hunt. 6.5.6 is not part of 6.5.5.

- There is some precedent for a referendum to be seperate from the effect that
calls the referendum. Granted, a referendum is almost always part of the
action that called it (i.e. in every case but the Blood Hunt), but there are
definitely two separate parts to a political action. The referendum is
resolved after the first part is completed. Saying that a Blood Hunt may be
called as part of a diablerie is not the same as saying that a Blood Hunt is
resolved as part of a diablerie. So, the rulebook does not specifically say
that the Blood Hunt *is* part of the diablerie.

- The fact that the Blood Hunt is not a part of the action strengthens the
point. If it is not part of the action that caused it to be called, then there
is reason to believe it is not part of the diablerie.

- In the absence of specific rulebook text to say that the Blood Hunt
*resolution* is part of the diablerie, one must go with the two things that
imply that the Blood Hunt is not a part (i.e. bullets 1 & 3 above).

However, I'm willing to just take this one as a screwed-up printing of the
rulebook that will be fixed in the next edition, because I really don't care
that much. I'm just happy that you reversed the extremely confusing ruling on
what effects are playable during a Blood Hunt. That was one added complexity
that I just really didn't think was necessary. With that reversal, the
question of whether the Blood Hunt is part of the diablerie or not just doesn't
matter.

What the whole argument has shown me is that you seem unlikely to listen to
anything I have to say. Perhaps you don't like me because I have argued with
your rulings so much in the past. If I actually have a point to make counter
to a ruling, I'll have to hope that someone else argues the point, as
tetragrammaton has in regards to the "treated like any other referendum"
phrase.

"only" that you have read into it.

Yes. As you continue to say. It doesn't, however say that. 5.5.5 says that a
blood hunt may be called. It neither implies nor states specifically that the
blood hunt is resolved at this point. Saying that this statement is enough to
require the blood hunt be part of the diablerie is equivalent, in my view, to
saying that a normal referendum is resolved as soon as one takes the action to
call it, whether successful or not. There are two parts to any normal
referendum... the part by which you call the referendum, and the part during
which the referendum is resolved. Granted, they are both part of the same
action, when called as a normal political action. In the case of the blood
hunt, only the first part of that whole rigamarole is actually declared to be
part of the diablerie. There are two ways to see the resolution grouped:

a) as part of the diablerie - since the effect to call the blood hunt is part
of the diablerie, the resolution of the blood hunt vote is assumed to be part
of the diablerie.

b) not part of the diablerie - since the blood hunt is listed as a separate
section, and because it is "not associated with any action", the blood hunt
vote is assumed to be separate from everything going on around it, and thus not
part of the diablerie. (Note: in one of my posts, I asked if "separate from
everything going on around it" included being separate from the diablerie, to
which you replied "OK.")

The only thing which seems to choose a) over b) is that you say so. Which is
fine. All I want is for you to say, "the blood hunt is part of the
diablerie... only because I say so, as the rules are not clear on this."
(Okay, okay, I said in a post above that I was gonna just give up and go away
anyway, but you know how hard it is to give up a debate, especially if the
other person seems like they might be starting to see what you're getting
at...)

> > in the rulebook mean anything at all, they imply grouping, no? If the
effect
> > described in 6 is part of the effect described in part 5, should it not be
> > numbered accordingly?
>
> Again (third, fourth time? I forget), see the section numbering for
> actions, combat, and political actions to see that the numbers don't
> mean what you want them to.
>

Assuming that's true (I'm not in the mood to look through the rules right now,
so I'll take your word that the numbering is completely random and doesn't mean
anything)... that's a poor way of organizing rules. If something is not a
logical part of something else, then it's okay for the numbers to not indicate
sequencing. When a phase or effect is meant to be a part of another phase or
effect, then the numbers should indicate that. Maybe the next rulebook
reprinting should take things like this into account.

Well the rules say that a successful action is the end, since you apply
effects at that point.

6.2.3
If the action is successful (all block attempts were unsuccessful), then
the cost of the action is paid, and the effects of the successful action

take place.

What happens after the effects take place? Can you then further modify
the action with a freak drive or other effects?

The action is apparently over once its been declared successful and you
apply the effects.

Now with regards to the Political referendum.

6.3.2. The Referendum

If a political action is successful, the referendum (sometimes referred
to as the vote*) is called.

This could be modified to read if a political action is unblocked, the
referendum () is called.

This allows the referendum to be a Part of the political action, but
removed enough from the action to allow the voting to proceed. This
returns the context of the cards to their original aspects, and you can
drop that whole paragraph that "allows" AMs/Reacts to be played in the
referendum, since with this change, the referendum is part of the
action.

I think that the following edits need to be made:

In section I there are sub-sections A, B, C, D, G, H?

Section II.A.1, I believe, has been clarified to mean "Untap *all*
cards you control. Unless some effect is preventing the untap, eg
Infernal."

Section II.A.3.c has been mis-edited to become part of II.A.3.b.iii.

Section II.C, it is not clear to me, by the sentence: "[6.5.2] NOTE:
Any time one of your vampires is ready during your minion phase and
has no blood and is not prevented from hunting, he must hunt
immediately." what happens if the minion has no blood and *is*
prevented from hunting, eg by NRA.

Section II.C.1, should read "Note: *Your* bleed actions...", perhaps a
comment should also be made that the (D) on bleed action cards is
reminder text of this fact, only.

Section II.C.8.b, state that the method of payment for the action
needs to be announced with the action.

Should the note at the end of Section II "NOTE: Only one out-of-turn
master card may be played in lieu of a Master Phase Action in your
next master phase." read "...in lieu of *each* Master Phase
Action..."? I'm not sure what the ruling is on this.

Section III.F.1, are definitions of action type required here?

Section IV.D specify when "during press step" effects are applied, eg
Dagon's Call.

To borrow contentious terms: are "press step", "damage resolution",
"determine blockers", "resolve diablerie" etc all atomic? If so,
could some general rulings be made about the timing of "During X"
type-cards when X is an atom.

Section VI is not too clear on aggravated damage. Perhaps, it should
be explicitly stated that the first point sends a vampire to torpor
(if not already there?) subsequent points burn either blood or the
vampire.

Generally, could examples be included? Perhaps, a companion document
of examples.

* lehrbuch

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Freak Drive is playable after the action is performed (card text, as
belabored already).

Just because it is only playable on an unlocked action (after that
successful action is performed) doesn't mean it is playable
immediately upon determining that the action is successful.

Trying to wiggle in some corner-cases for fizzled actions (which
are unblocked but then not resolved at all for some reason,
like having no acting minion around or not being able to pay the
cost) is not going to change the fact that FD is played after the
action is performed, although it does illustrate that some
actions can be unblocked and still not resolve (so not be successful).

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
rai...@spamcop.net writes:

>Thats the crux of the problem, you continue to state the diablery is
>indivisible, then tell us that you can play outside effects to change
>the outcome of the diablery and blood hunt.

Indivisible means the components cannot be separated from
one another, and that effects cannot be played inbetween the
components. You can modify the components, and *of course*
if one of the components includes the possibility of sub-events
those sub-events don't "divide" the component. Playing
vote modifiers in the middle of a referendum doesn't "divide"
it, and since other effects are in general allowable, they
don't either.

IMO for sensible behavior of RotBR the bloodhunt *should*
be divided from the rest of the diablerie. That's the intuitive
understanding anyway. It is, technically a rules change
although I don't think it's incompatibly with the current
printed rules.

If RotBR modified the blood transfer I wouldn't consider
it "interrupting" the diablerie either.
